task.title: Claim the next due schedule through deterministic CLI JSON
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/843 by exposing kernel-owned deterministic next-due reservation without widening CLI authority.
acceptance_criteria: Delegate one exact caller cutoff to ScheduleStore::claim_next_due.
Emit the complete claimed projection or explicit null when no work is eligible.
Fail closed with schedule_claim_failed and no partial stdout, clock, dispatch, materialization, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: CLI tests failed because claim-next was not a recognized subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the required success, absence or conflict, validation, and fail-closed paths.

attempts.summary: Implemented the bounded contract and refactored only demonstrated duplication.
attempts.diagnostic: The deterministic operation existed only in the kernel, while CLI callers otherwise had to recreate selection and widen the race surface.
attempts.patch: Added the command and optional output wrapper, reused complete schedule projection, and covered deterministic selection, absence, and corruption.

attempts.summary: Fixed the substantive review finding and waited for exact-head review.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit found that the README omitted schedule_claim_failed and the no-partial-stdout guarantee; the first incremental review of the fix was rate limited.
attempts.patch: Documented the stable failure contract, resolved the thread, kept auto-merge disabled through the cooldown, and resumed review only after the shared budget allowed it.

outcome.summary: CLI callers can atomically reserve earliest due work without recreating selection policy or receiving execution authority.

lessons: Expose one kernel selection operation instead of a list-then-claim race in scripts.
Document stable failure diagnostics and no-partial-stdout behavior as part of the automation contract.
A rate-limited CodeRabbit status is false green; resume after cooldown and require genuine exact-head review before merge.
